high.title: Prabowo's Advisor Reveals Unavoidable Layoffs: 2,500 Workers at PT Pakerin to Lose Jobs
high.summary: PT Pakerin in Mojokerto, East Java is confirmed to undergo mass layoffs affecting 2,500 workers. The Indonesia Deposit Insurance Corporation (LPS) has identified approximately IDR 159 billion in PT Pakerin funds held at Bank Prima to be disbursed for severance payments. This signals continued stress in Indonesia's manufacturing sector and raises concerns about broader industrial employment conditions.

high.title: New Outsourcing Rules to Be Issued in July: Only 4 Job Types Permitted for Contract Workers
high.summary: A revised Ministerial Regulation (Permenaker No. 7/2026) on outsourcing is set to be released by mid-July 2026, fundamentally restricting the use of contract/outsourced workers in Indonesian companies. Only four support roles — catering staff, security, drivers, and cleaning services — will be exempt, with companies given a 6-month compliance window. This regulatory shift has significant implications for labor-intensive industries and companies reliant on flexible workforce arrangements.

high.title: Prabowo Plans to Close 750 State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) That Are Unprofitable and Only Paying Overhead
high.summary: President Prabowo Subianto announced plans to shut down approximately 750 state-owned enterprises (SOEs) that have failed to generate profit while continuing to incur large overhead costs including directors' and commissioners' salaries. This sweeping SOE restructuring initiative signals a major shift in Indonesia's state enterprise policy aimed at improving fiscal efficiency. The move could have significant implications for the broader SOE sector, including listed state-owned companies on the Indonesian Stock Exchange.

high.title: Leaked: Tomorrow DPR and Government to Discuss Mining Work Plan and Budget (RKAB), Triggering Mass Layoff Fears
high.summary: A critical coordination meeting between the Indonesian parliament (DPR) and government is scheduled for June 30 to address unresolved Mining Work Plan and Budget (RKAB) approvals. With 90% of mining operations currently halted due to pending RKAB approvals and production quota cuts, hundreds of thousands of workers face potential layoffs. The crisis also impacts supporting sectors including heavy equipment, dump trucks, and other ancillary services, making this a significant systemic risk to Indonesia's mining industry.

high.title: Government to Take Over PT Granito if Company Refuses to Continue Operations Despite Gas Price Reduction
high.summary: The Indonesian government has decided to intervene and take over PT Granito if the company refuses to resume operations despite a reduction in industrial gas prices, signaling an unprecedented level of state intervention in private business. Two options are being considered: acquisition through the state investment vehicle Danantara or finding a new investor, with 447 workers already affected by layoffs. This move sets a notable precedent for government policy on handling industrial closures and labor disputes.

high.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Confirms Marketplaces to Collect Online Merchant Taxes Starting July
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa confirmed that domestic e-commerce platforms will be appointed as collectors of Income Tax (PPh) Article 22 on merchant sales transactions starting July 2026. The policy aims to create a level playing field between online and offline traders, with the mechanism shifting from self-reporting by online merchants to marketplace-collected withholding tax. This regulatory change will directly impact major e-commerce platforms and their merchant ecosystems in Indonesia.

high.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Responds to Labor Unions' Request to Abolish JHT Pension Fund Tax
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa responded to labor union protests demanding the removal of income tax on BPJS Ketenagakerjaan pension fund (JHT) disbursements, stating the government will review the policy and benchmark against international best practices. Purbaya raised fairness concerns, suggesting that eliminating the tax could disproportionately benefit wealthier individuals. The existing tax regulation dates back to Government Regulation No. 68/2009 and has significant implications for millions of Indonesian workers and the broader social security system.

high.title: Leaked: Tomorrow DPR and Government to Discuss Mining Work Plan Budget (RKAB), Threatening Hundreds of Thousands of Layoffs
high.summary: The Indonesian Confederation of Trade Unions (KSPSI) has warned that 90% of mining operations have halted due to unresolved Mining Work Plan and Budget (RKAB) approvals, threatening hundreds of thousands of workers with layoffs. An emergency coordination meeting between the government and parliament is scheduled for June 30 to address the crisis. The widespread operational stoppage is already cascading into supporting sectors including heavy equipment, dump trucks, and other mining services.

high.title: Government to Take Over PT Granito if Company Refuses to Continue Operations Despite Gas Price Reduction
high.summary: The Indonesian government has decided to intervene and take over PT Granito if the company refuses to resume operations following a reduction in industrial gas prices, signaling a significant shift toward direct state intervention in struggling private enterprises. Two rescue mechanisms are being considered: acquisition through the Danantara sovereign wealth fund or sourcing a new investor. This development follows the layoff of 447 workers and sets a precedent for potential government takeovers of companies facing closure.

high.title: JCI Closes Down 1.28%, Remains Below 6,000
high.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) closed sharply lower at 5,820, falling 75 points or 1.28% on Monday, June 29, 2026, remaining stuck below the 6,000 level. The index had opened in positive territory at 5,932 but reversed course, hitting an intraday low of 5,800. This continued weakness signals sustained bearish sentiment in the Indonesian equity market and may concern investors holding domestic equities.

high.title: Indonesian Capital Market Threatened with Demotion from Emerging Markets to Frontier Markets, New BEI Chief Responds
high.summary: MSCI's 2026 Market Classification Review has flagged Indonesia's capital market as at risk of being downgraded from Emerging Markets to Frontier Markets status in its November review. A potential downgrade would likely trigger significant capital outflows as global funds tracking Emerging Market indices would be forced to divest Indonesian holdings. BEI's new President Director Jeffrey Hendrik acknowledged the threat, emphasizing that MSCI is waiting for consistent implementation of ongoing capital market reforms.

medium.title: DJP Appoints 7 New Digital Tax Collectors Including Strava and Kling AI
medium.summary: Indonesia's Directorate General of Taxes (DJP) has designated seven new entities as VAT collectors for Electronic System Trade (PMSE) as of May 2026, including Strava Inc, Envato, Nielsen Norman Group, Kling AI, and others. This reflects Indonesia's ongoing expansion of its digital economy tax net, covering fitness, digital content, education, and AI services. Investors should note the government's continued commitment to monetizing the digital economy through taxation.

medium.title: Prabowo's Advisor Calls for Zero Tax on BPJS Employment Pension Fund (JHT) Withdrawals
medium.summary: Presidential Special Advisor Said Iqbal has proposed that income tax (PPh) on JHT pension fund withdrawals be set to 0%, arguing that taxing JHT payouts constitutes double taxation since workers' wages are already taxed under PPh Article 21. If adopted, this policy change would directly impact government tax revenue and benefit millions of Indonesian formal sector workers. The proposal adds to a series of labor-friendly policy signals from the Prabowo administration.

medium.title: Broiler Chicken Farmers Cry Out as Farm-Gate Prices Plunge to IDR 13,000/kg
medium.summary: Live broiler chicken prices at the farm level have dropped sharply to IDR 13,000–14,000/kg in West Java, well below break-even costs, with the decline ongoing since April 2026. The Permindo poultry farmers association describes this as the worst price crash experienced, threatening the viability of independent poultry farms. This trend is relevant for agribusiness investors and companies in the poultry supply chain, including feed producers and integrated poultry companies listed on the IDX.

medium.title: Revealed: Japanese Automotive Giants from Yazaki Group That Planned to Leave Indonesia — But Were Stopped
medium.summary: PT JAI in Pasuruan and PT SAI in Mojokerto, both part of Japan's Yazaki Group, have scaled back plans to relocate 50% of their production lines to Vietnam following dialogue between management and labor unions. Only 3 to 5 production lines will now be relocated instead of the originally planned large-scale shift. This development is significant for Indonesia's automotive components sector and highlights ongoing foreign investment retention challenges.

medium.title: Customs Intercepts Thai National Carrying USD 350,000 (Rp 6.3 Billion) in Cash at Soekarno-Hatta Airport
medium.summary: Indonesian Customs at Soekarno-Hatta Airport intercepted a Thai national carrying USD 350,000 in cash without proper authorization at the international arrivals terminal, as part of efforts to maintain monetary stability and financial sovereignty. The funds are now secured at the Customs office while further investigations into corporate financial compliance are underway. This case underscores Indonesia's tightening enforcement of cross-border cash carrying regulations.

medium.title: Ministry of Transportation Speaks Out on the Future of High-Speed Rail Extension to Surabaya
medium.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Transportation has indicated no immediate commitment to extending the Whoosh high-speed rail beyond Bandung to Surabaya, stating that the government's current priority is completing the financial restructuring of the existing Jakarta-Bandung high-speed rail project. The statement aligns with directions from Coordinating Minister AHY, who chairs the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Rail Committee. This signals continued uncertainty around the expansion project and its related investment opportunities.

medium.title: Tax Authority Appoints 7 New Digital Tax Collectors Including Strava
medium.summary: Indonesia's Directorate General of Taxes (DJP) has appointed seven new entities as VAT collectors for Electronic System Trade (PMSE), including Strava Inc, Envato, Kling AI, and others operating in fitness, digital content, education, and AI sectors. This is part of Indonesia's ongoing effort to capture tax revenue from the growing digital economy. The expansion of digital VAT collection reflects the government's continued push to broaden the tax base from foreign digital service providers.

medium.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Comments After Government Receives 30-Hectare Land Grant in Meikarta
medium.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa praised Lippo Group's donation of approximately 30 hectares of land in the Meikarta development area to support the government's 3 million homes construction program. The handover, signed at the Danantara building, reflects growing private sector participation in one of President Prabowo's flagship Asta Cita agenda items. This is significant for investors in property and housing sectors as it signals continued momentum behind the government's large-scale affordable housing initiative.

medium.title: Presidential Advisor Proposes Zero Tax on JHT (Old Age Security) Pension Withdrawals, Citing Double Taxation on Workers
medium.summary: Presidential Special Advisor for Labor Affairs Said Iqbal has proposed eliminating income tax on BPJS Ketenagakerjaan JHT (old age security fund) withdrawals, arguing that workers are being taxed twice as their salaries are already subject to Article 21 income tax. A formal letter is expected to be sent to the Finance Minister to discuss zeroing out taxes on JHT, severance pay, pension benefits, and holiday allowances (THR). If adopted, this policy change could significantly benefit Indonesian workers and affect state tax revenue calculations.

medium.title: Cancel a GoCar Ride and Get Charged Rp 3,000 — Here Are the Details
medium.summary: GoTo's ride-hailing platform Gojek has introduced a Rp 3,000 cancellation fee for GoCar orders, applicable to all GoCar services except GoCar Instant and GoCar Rental. The policy has been rolled out gradually since February 3 in major cities including Bali, Surabaya, Yogyakarta, Medan, Bandung, Malang, and Makassar. This monetization move by GOTO (IDX: GOTO) could improve unit economics for its ride-hailing segment and is relevant to investors tracking the company's path to profitability.

medium.title: LPDP Opens Phase II Scholarship Registration from June 30 to July 31
medium.summary: Indonesia's Education Fund Management Institution (LPDP) is opening Phase II scholarship registrations from June 30 to July 31, 2026, with at least 80% of allocations focused on STEM and strategic industries including AI, semiconductors, food, energy, and manufacturing. The program reflects the government's continued investment in human capital development aligned with national industrial priorities. This initiative supports Indonesia's long-term economic competitiveness by funding advanced education in critical sectors.

medium.title: Finance Minister Praises Lippo Group's Donation of 30 Hectares of Meikarta Land to Government for 3 Million Homes Program
medium.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa welcomed Lippo Group's donation of approximately 30 hectares of land in the Meikarta development area to the government, supporting President Prabowo's priority program to build and renovate 3 million homes. The land handover was formalized through a signing ceremony at Wisma Danantara, highlighting cooperation between the state and private sector. This move is significant for PT Lippo Cikarang Tbk (LPCK) investors as it represents a major asset transfer and demonstrates the company's engagement with the national housing agenda.

medium.title: Presidential Advisor Proposes Zero Tax on BPJS Employment JHT Withdrawals, Arguing Workers Are Taxed Twice
medium.summary: Presidential Special Advisor for Labor Affairs Said Iqbal has proposed eliminating income tax on JHT (old-age benefit) withdrawals from BPJS Ketenagakerjaan, arguing that taxing these payouts constitutes double taxation since workers' wages are already subject to income tax (PPh 21). He plans to formally submit the proposal to the Finance Minister, extending the request to cover severance pay, pension benefits, and holiday allowances (THR) as well. If implemented, this policy change would directly benefit millions of Indonesian workers and reduce overall tax burdens on labor-related payouts.

medium.title: BEI Chief Sets Ambitious Target of 1,100 New Listed Companies by 2030
medium.summary: Newly appointed BEI President Director Jeffrey Hendrik has set ambitious targets for the 2026-2030 period, including growing market capitalization to IDR 30,000 trillion and achieving an average daily transaction value of IDR 31 trillion. The exchange also targets adding 1,100 new listed companies over the five-year period. These targets reflect BEI's long-term growth ambitions, though they stand in contrast to the current market weakness and MSCI downgrade risk.

medium.title: BEI Chief Responds to Ministry of Finance and Danantara Potentially Holding Exchange Shares
medium.summary: BEI is awaiting implementing regulations under the Financial Sector Development and Strengthening (P2SK) Law, which would allow government institutions including the Ministry of Finance, Bank Indonesia, and BPI Danantara to become shareholders of the exchange through demutualization. President Director Jeffrey Hendrik confirmed full support for the demutualization process and ongoing coordination with all relevant parties. This structural ownership change could have significant implications for BEI's governance and independence going forward.

medium.title: Official: Jeffrey Hendrik Appointed as New President Director of Indonesia Stock Exchange
medium.summary: Jeffrey Hendrik was officially appointed as BEI's President Director for the 2026-2030 term at the Annual General Meeting of Shareholders (RUPST) held on Monday, June 29, 2026. Previously serving as Acting President Director, Hendrik outlined his vision to elevate BEI into the top 10 global exchanges by market capitalization and transaction value, up from its current rankings of 19th and 17th respectively. His leadership comes at a critical time as the exchange faces both MSCI downgrade risks and ambitious growth targets.
